title: bug: moe-proxy `npm test` (pretest → build → clean) deletes the shared proxy dist before tsc can start, so one WSL test run breaks every new seat's MCP bridge
description:
Found 2026-10-30 19:05Z. architect-bc59d28a flagged it while planning task-f9789178 (comment-e121954d), and the governor verified it read-only. This is the same class of bug as f9789178, but in packages/moe-proxy and packages/moe-claude-plugin, and the proxy trigger is more routine.

Mechanism:
- packages/moe-proxy/package.json: `pretest` = `npm run build`, `prebuild` = `npm run clean` (rmSync dist), `build` = `tsc`.
- So a plain `npm test` in packages/moe-proxy deletes dist first. CLAUDE.md lists that as a routine command.
- In the shared checkout, node_modules is a Windows install. From WSL, tsc then throws "Unable to resolve @typescript/typescript-linux-x64" (the TypeScript 7 native build). The run ends with no proxy dist at all.
- scripts/moe-agent.sh:722/1779 (and the .ps1 twin) launch `$ROOT_DIR/packages/moe-proxy/dist/index.js` for every seat. Proxies already running keep their loaded code. But workers and QA respawn a fresh CLI per task, so within minutes every new seat would fail to bridge MCP to the daemon.
- packages/moe-claude-plugin has the same clean-first `prebuild`. Its dist is not committed and its hook fails open, so the impact is lower. Fix it the same way for consistency.

Fix (mirror f9789178's landed shape): a build that cannot compile must leave an existing dist alone. Minimum: `prebuild` runs `tsc --version && npm run clean`. TypeScript 7's bin/tsc resolves its native platform package first, so it exits non-zero before clean when the compiler cannot start. A stronger variant is allowed if it stays small: tsc into a temp outDir, then rename. tsc emits despite type errors (noEmitOnError unset), so a type error still rebuilds dist.
definitionOfDone: packages/moe-proxy/package.json and packages/moe-claude-plugin/package.json: when the compiler cannot start, `npm run build` (and therefore the proxy's `npm test` via pretest) exits non-zero and leaves an existing dist/ untouched; `clean` (or any rm of dist) runs only after a compiler start check succeeds. Windows `npm run build` in a clean clone still produces a complete dist for both packages, with git status --porcelain empty afterwards.

A vitest test in packages/moe-proxy reads both package.json files and fails if `clean` or any rm of dist can run before the compiler start check. A scratch mutant that restores the old clean-first order proves it RED.

Evidence that the failure mode is gone: in a scratch COPY outside the shared checkout, with a marker at packages/moe-proxy/dist/.keep, a WSL `npm test` against Windows-native node_modules exits non-zero AND dist/.keep still exists. `npm test` exits 0 for both packages in a fresh snapshot (Linux snapshot with its own npm ci, or native Windows clone).
taskRails: Never run `npm test`, `npm run build`, `npm run clean`, `npm ci` or `npm install` in the shared checkout D:\projexts\moes (or /mnt/d/projexts/moes) for ANY package. Every seat launches packages/moe-proxy/dist and the live daemon runs from packages/moe-daemon/dist. Use a git archive or clone snapshot outside the repo for every build or verification step.
Scope: packages/moe-proxy/package.json, packages/moe-claude-plugin/package.json, plus one small test file in packages/moe-proxy. No daemon, launcher or CI change.

implementationPlan.description:
TEST FIRST (RED). Create packages/moe-proxy/src/buildScriptOrder.test.ts (about 100 lines). Helpers stay inside the test file: no production module, no other file. Header comment: every seat's MCP bridge runs packages/moe-proxy/dist, so a build must not delete dist unless the compiler can start. task-a10a7f78: from WSL, the shared checkout's Windows-native node_modules has no linux tsc, so the proxy's `npm test` (pretest -> build -> clean) deleted dist before tsc failed.
Manifests: read both the way packages/moe-daemon/src/server/McpAdapter.test.ts:109 reads its manifest. Use JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(new URL('../package.json', import.meta.url), 'utf8')).scripts, and the same for '../../moe-claude-plugin/package.json'. Key them 'moe-proxy' and 'moe-claude-plugin'.
Helpers: copy splitSteps and runOrder verbatim from the landed packages/moe-daemon/src/util/buildScriptOrder.test.ts. That is task-f9789178, which must be DONE before this row can be claimed. Make one change: the nested-script regex becomes /^npm (?:run|run-script) ([\w:-]+)$/, so colon names such as test:coverage expand too. If f9789178's QA loop changed the helpers or its remover/probe regexes, mirror the landed version and say so in the step note.
Classifiers:
- isProbe: exactly `tsc --version` or `tsc -v`.
- isEmit: `tsc` or `tsc <args>` that is not a probe.
- removesDist: the daemon test's case-insensitive whole-word remover regex (rmSync|rmdirSync|rimraf|rm|rmdir|del|rd|Remove-Item) AND its `dist` path-token regex.
orderViolations(scripts): string[]
(a) Every script name except `clean` is an entry point; skip keys whose value is undefined. For each entry, leaves = runOrder(scripts, name). Every removal leaf with no probe leaf before it yields `"<name>" runs "<leaf>" before tsc --version`. Only `clean` is exempt, because running it is a deliberate delete.
(b) On runOrder(scripts, 'build'):
- 'build never removes dist' when there is no removal. Clean must still run, so outputs of deleted sources do not linger, and so the check cannot pass vacuously if the remover regex ever misses.
- 'build never emits with tsc' when there is no emit.
- 'build emits with tsc before dist is removed' when an emit precedes the last removal.
Error handling: splitSteps and runOrder throw descriptive errors: the script name and operator, or recursion depth 8. orderViolations catches any error and returns its message as the single violation, so the suite does not crash. An unreadable or invalid package.json fails the test with the fs or JSON error.
Type-check constraint: the proxy tsconfig compiles all of src, tests included, into dist at target ES2022, and pretest runs that build. A type error therefore fails `npm test`. Use no ES2023+ API: no findLastIndex, findLast or toSorted (the daemon test's findLastIndex does not type-check here). .at(), lastIndexOf and flatMap are fine.
Cases:
(1) it.each(Object.entries(manifests)) '%s probes tsc before anything removes dist' -> toEqual([]).
(2) it.each rows over { ...proxyScripts, prebuild: 'tsc --version && npm run clean', ...override }. Each asserts toContainEqual(expect.stringContaining(needle)):
- {prebuild:'npm run clean'} -> '"test" runs' (proves the pretest path)
- {pretest:'npm run clean && npm run build'} -> '"pretest" runs'
- {prestart:'rimraf dist'} -> '"start" runs "rimraf dist"'
- {prebuild:'tsc --version'} -> 'build never removes dist'
- {build:undefined} -> 'build never emits'
- {prebuild:'tsc --version', build:'tsc && npm run clean'} -> 'emits with tsc before'
- {prebuild:'npm run-script clean && tsc --version && npm run clean'} -> 'before tsc --version'
- {clean:'npm run clean'} -> 'recursion depth 8'
- prebuild 'tsc --version <op> npm run clean', for each op in ; | || & -> 'chains steps with "<op>"'
- clean = each of: rm -rf ./dist/, rimraf "dist", rmdir /s /q dist, del dist\* (the TS literal doubles the backslash), rd dist, Remove-Item -Recurse dist, and a node -e rmdirSync('dist') one-liner. Each with prebuild 'npm run clean' -> 'before tsc --version'.
(3) Accepts prebuild 'tsc -v && npm run clean' plus postbuild `node -e "console.log('a;b|c&d')"` -> toEqual([]).
I prototyped exactly this in a scratch archive: 22 cases. On HEAD's manifests only the two real-manifest cases fail. The proxy lists prebuild, build, pretest, test, pretest:coverage, test:coverage and prepublishOnly; the plugin lists prebuild, build and prepublishOnly. Every row passes, and `npx tsc --noEmit -p .` returns rc 0. The project's globalRails forbiddenPatterns apply to this file, comments and strings included.

The daemon is included because src/workerType.integration.test.ts imports its source.
- For each of moe-daemon, moe-proxy and moe-claude-plugin, open a subshell that starts with `cd "$SNAP/repo/packages/<pkg>" || exit 1`, then run `env -i HOME=$HOME PATH=/home/sysadmin/.nvm/versions/node/v24.21.0/bin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin npm ci --no-audit --no-fund`.
- Overlay ONLY the new test (cp + cmp).
- From $SNAP/repo/packages/moe-proxy, with the same env -i prefix plus NO_COLOR=1, run `npx tsc --noEmit -p .` -> rc 0. Then run `npx vitest run src/buildScriptOrder.test.ts` -> rc 1. Exactly the two real-manifest cases fail, and every row passes.

implementationPlan.description:
FIX. In packages/moe-proxy/package.json and packages/moe-claude-plugin/package.json, change ONLY scripts.prebuild from `npm run clean` to `tsc --version && npm run clean`. Every other byte stays: clean, build = tsc, pretest, pretest:coverage, prepublishOnly, 2-space JSON, LF and the final newline. `git diff` shows exactly one -/+ line pair per file.
Why (repeat this in the step note): TypeScript 7.0.2's bin/tsc imports lib/tsc.js, and that calls getExePath() (lib/getExePath.js) before anything else.
- When the native platform package is missing, getExePath() throws 'Unable to resolve @typescript/typescript-<platform>-<arch>'.
- Otherwise tsc.js execs the native binary for every argv, --version included. So the probe starts the same executable that build's `tsc` uses, through the same node_modules/.bin resolution.
I checked this read-only in the shared checkout on 2026-10-30. From WSL, `node_modules/.bin/tsc --version` gives rc=1 with that error in both packages. On Windows, `node_modules\.bin\tsc --version` prints 'Version 7.0.2', rc=0.
Clean stays right before build's tsc. Stale outputs of deleted sources are still removed, and a type error still rebuilds dist (noEmitOnError is unset). The proxy's pretest and pretest:coverage reach the fixed prebuild through `npm run build`; leave them alone.
Do not touch packages/moe-daemon (task-f9789178's), launchers, CI, docs or the IDE-bundled copies.
Overlay both edited manifests into $SNAP (cp + cmp) and rerun step 1's vitest command: every case passes.

Reused landed daemon's minimal tsc --version && clean pattern; no dependency or abstraction. Read TypeScript 7.0.2 bin/tsc -> lib/tsc.js -> getExePath(): native platform package resolution throws Unable to resolve @typescript/typescript-<platform>-<arch> before clean; successful resolution execs the same native binary even for --version through the same node_modules/.bin as emit. Clean remains immediately before tsc, stale outputs removed, noEmitOnError remains unset; pretest/pretest:coverage unchanged. cp+cmp overlays of both manifests into Linux snapshot; focused vitest rc=0, 22/22 pass (/tmp/moe-a10a-evidence/green-test.log). No daemon/launcher/CI/docs/IDE edits.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
(1) Chosen: prebuild = `tsc --version && npm run clean` in both packages. This is the shape task-f9789178 landed for the daemon, minus its generators: one line each, with no new failure mode.
(2) tsc into a temp outDir, then rename. Rejected for f9789178's reasons: Windows has no atomic directory swap, so it is still rm + rename, and renaming freshly written trees fails with EPERM/EBUSY under AV or indexers. It is also more moving parts than the scope rail allows.
(3) Drop clean. Rejected: outputs of deleted sources would linger in dist, the npm tarball and the IDE bundles.
(4) Drop the proxy's `pretest: npm run build`. Rejected: it changes what `npm test` proves, and the DoD keeps the build in the test path.
(5) Pin only the build lifecycle, as the daemon test does. Rejected: the proxy's routine trigger is `npm test` or `test:coverage` through pretest. Checking every script except `clean` covers every entry point, and the RED output names each one.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
Both packages install TypeScript 7.0.2; the shared checkout has only @typescript/typescript-win32-x64. bin/tsc imports lib/tsc.js, which resolves the native platform package through lib/getExePath.js before doing anything. It then execs the native binary even for --version, so `tsc --version` starts the same executable the emit uses. I checked this read-only on 2026-10-30: from WSL, rc=1 with 'Unable to resolve @typescript/typescript-linux-x64' in both packages; on Windows, 'Version 7.0.2', rc=0.
npm runs pre/post hooks for any script name, colon names included (pretest:coverage), and also for a nested `npm run x`.
The proxy's tsconfig compiles all of src, *.test.ts included, into dist at target ES2022, and pretest runs that build. The new test must therefore type-check without ES2023 APIs: the daemon test's findLastIndex would fail here.
The plugin's dist is gitignored and absent from the shared checkout, and its hook fails open.
My prototype, in a scratch archive outside the repo:
- The described test has 22 cases. It is RED on HEAD's manifests (the two real-manifest cases fail; every row passes) and GREEN after the one-line fixes.
- Proxy `npm test` passes 7 files / 312 tests. The plugin builds and passes 2 files / 18 tests.
- With the Linux TypeScript package moved aside, new-order `npm test` exits rc=1 and keeps dist/.keep and dist/index.js. The old order also exits rc=1, but deletes dist.
planningNotes.risks:
- Any npm or npx command in /mnt/d/projexts/moes can delete the live proxy or daemon dist. Run every build and test in $SNAP or $W, behind `cd <dir> || exit 1` or a subshell that starts with it.
- Call cmd.exe only from a /mnt/d cwd, and strip carriage returns before diffing.
- sed: & in a replacement means the whole match. Edit only in the new->old direction, and restore with cp + cmp or git checkout.
- f9789178's helpers may change during its QA loop. Mirror what landed.
- Peer WIP can turn the proxy or plugin suite red at HEAD. Prove it on a plain HEAD archive and block on the owning row; never edit their files.
- Residual, to state but not fix: a tsc crash mid-emit after clean still leaves a partial dist. A Windows in-place build of the shared checkout still succeeds and compiles peers' WIP into the live dist, so the global customRule against building the shared checkout stands.
